finding.claim: The plugin defaults `dotfiles` to 'allow'. This overrides the safer @fastify/send default of 'ignore'. With default options, dotfiles and dot-directories under the static root are served to anonymous clients. Examples are `.env`, `.git/config`, `.htpasswd` and `.npmrc`. The user never opted in to this. This weakens a secure-by-default control.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET/HEAD to `<prefix>/.env`, `/.git/config` or any other dotfile path, on a deployment that did not set `dotfiles`.
finding.sink: `send(request.raw, encodeURI(pathnameForSend), options)` at index.js:302 streams the file via `reply.send(stream)` at index.js:439.

trace.note: `opts.dotfiles ??= 'allow'` sets the default to allow when the option is unset
`dotfiles: opts.dotfiles` is copied into `sendOptions`, so @fastify/send's own default of 'ignore' is never applied
The wildcard GET/HEAD route handler takes the request path
The file stream is sent to the client

finding.guards_checked: The dot-dot traversal guards (index.js:262 and :769) only stop `..` segments, not dotfile names. `allowedPath` is optional and unset by default. The dirList dotfile filter (dirList.js:83) only hides entries in listings and does not block direct requests. The non-wildcard mode uses glob `dot: opts.serveDotFiles`, but `dotfiles:'allow'` still applies when serving.
